name: YarnSpinnerTool/YarnSpinner
description: Yarn Spinner is a friendly, screenplay-like tool for writing branching dialogue in games, used in Night in the Woods, A Short Hike, and Dredge. Supports Unity, Godot, and Rust integrations.
score_rationale: Industry-recognized dialogue framework used in many successful indie games, actively maintained with 2.7k stars and a growing cross-engine ecosystem.

name: klembot/twinejs
description: Twine is an open-source tool for creating interactive, nonlinear stories without coding, publishing directly to HTML. The most widely used interactive fiction authoring platform with multiple story formats.
score_rationale: Dominant interactive fiction authoring tool with 2.7k stars, widely used in education and indie game development, actively maintained through late 2025.

name: inkle/inky
description: The official IDE for the ink narrative scripting language, featuring a live play-through editor, syntax highlighting, real-time error detection, and JSON export. Essential companion to the ink runtime.
score_rationale: The primary authoring tool for ink with 2.6k stars, tightly integrated with the ink ecosystem and used in professional game development workflows.

name: ganelson/inform
description: Inform 7 is a programming language for creating interactive fiction using natural language syntax, one of the most influential IF authoring systems. Open-sourced in 2022 after decades of commercial use.
score_rationale: One of the most historically significant interactive fiction languages with 1.6k stars, used in academia and by serious IF authors, open-sourced and actively maintained.

name: mhgolkar/Arrow
description: Arrow is a free open-source game narrative design tool built on Godot for creating text adventures, interactive stories, and visual novels. Features a visual node editor and HTML export.
score_rationale: Strong 1.3k star narrative design tool with active maintenance through 2025, offering an accessible visual approach to game storytelling.

name: YarnSpinnerTool/YarnSpinner-Unity
description: The official Unity integration for Yarn Spinner, providing components, editors, and runtime support for branching dialogue in Unity games. Used in Night in the Woods and A Short Hike.
score_rationale: Official Unity integration for the popular Yarn Spinner framework with 749 stars, actively maintained into late 2025.

name: inkle/ink-unity-integration
description: Official Unity package for integrating the ink narrative scripting language, supporting automatic compilation, a story player window, and full C# API access for controlling narratives in Unity games.
score_rationale: Official ink-Unity bridge with 682 stars and strong adoption among Unity developers building narrative games.

name: devdogio/Quest-System-Pro
description: A previously commercial Unity quest and conversation tree system, now open-sourced, featuring built-in quest types (gather, kill, talk), conversation trees, achievements, and NPC waypoint behavior.
score_rationale: Mature, feature-rich Unity quest and dialogue system with 642 stars, formerly on the Asset Store and now freely open-sourced.

name: Kirilllive/tuesday-js
description: Tuesday JS is a free, browser-based visual novel editor using standard HTML5 elements with no dependencies. Supports SVG, GIF animations, CSS styling and exports to desktop and Android.
score_rationale: Accessible no-dependency visual novel tool with 636 stars, actively maintained through 2026 and suitable for web-first interactive fiction projects.

name: NotYetGames/DlgSystem
description: A free, source-available dialogue plugin for Unreal Engine 5 with graph-based editing, Blueprint and C++ support, event/condition systems, and plain-text import/export. Used in commercial titles like The Ascent.
score_rationale: Well-established Unreal Engine dialogue plugin with 597 stars, actively maintained for UE 5.x, proven in commercial game development.

name: liana-p/narrat-engine
description: Narrat is a TypeScript/Vue game engine for building interactive narrative RPGs with skill checks, inventory, quests, and a scripting syntax for branching dialogue and story flow.
score_rationale: A dedicated narrative RPG engine with a complete feature set, though modest community size at 177 stars; a solid niche tool for browser-based narrative games.

name: Mountea-Framework/MounteaDialogueSystem
description: An open-source Unreal Engine plugin for building complex dialogue trees with a visual graph editor, validation, real-time preview, and decorator-based event triggers for cutscenes.
score_rationale: Actively maintained Unreal dialogue plugin through 2026 with 360 stars, offering strong editor tooling for complex narrative scenarios.

name: inkle/ink-library
description: A curated collection of ink code samples, tools, engine ports (Unity, JS, Godot, Rust), editor extensions, and a list of games built with ink. The central resource hub for the ink ecosystem.
score_rationale: Essential reference repository for the ink narrative ecosystem with 319 stars, cataloging ports, tools, and real-world usage examples.

name: microsoft/jericho
description: A lightweight Python interface connecting reinforcement learning agents with interactive fiction games, enabling AI research on text-based adventure game environments.
score_rationale: Valuable research platform for AI and interactive fiction with 322 stars, actively maintained through 2025 by Microsoft Research.

name: YarnSpinnerTool/YarnSpinner-Rust
description: A Rust implementation of Yarn Spinner with first-class Bevy game engine support, enabling dialogue systems in Rust-based games with full Yarn Spinner script compatibility.
score_rationale: Official Rust/Bevy port of the popular Yarn Spinner dialogue system with 273 stars, actively maintained through 2026 as Rust game dev grows.

name: tajmone/awesome-interactive-fiction
description: A comprehensive curated list of interactive fiction frameworks, tools, interpreters, authoring systems, and community resources covering all major IF platforms and languages.
score_rationale: Valuable discovery resource for the IF ecosystem with 206 stars, useful as a meta-catalog but not a tool or engine itself.

name: textadventures/quest
description: Quest Viva is an open-source platform for creating and playing text adventure games without programming experience, supporting multimedia and cross-platform play via web and desktop.
score_rationale: Actively maintained accessible text adventure engine with 333 stars, targeting non-programmers and maintaining regular releases into 2026.

name: SkyAphid/ClearDialogue
description: A free open-source engine-agnostic branching dialogue editor for video games, built with Java, featuring node-based editing and JSON export for any game engine integration.
score_rationale: Engine-agnostic branching dialogue editor with only 34 stars, last updated in 2019 — effectively abandoned and superseded by more active tools.

name: skypjack/entt
description: Header-only C++20 ECS library providing a fast sparse-set based entity component system, RTTI, reflection, resource management, event handling, and scheduling. Used in Minecraft (Mojang) and ArcGIS Runtime SDKs.
score_rationale: Industry-leading C++ ECS with 12.4k stars, MIT licensed, actively maintained through December 2024, and production-proven by Minecraft's Bedrock Edition — the benchmark for C++ ECS performance.

name: SanderMertens/flecs
description: Fast entity component system for C and C++ supporting millions of entities with archetype-based storage, hierarchies, prefabs, queries, and a pipeline system. Includes a built-in REST API and explorer UI.
score_rationale: One of the most featured and actively maintained ECS frameworks with 8.1k stars, MIT licensed, updated through March 2026, and uniquely offering built-in tooling like an ECS explorer.

name: sschmid/Entitas
description: Super fast ECS framework for C# and Unity with code generation that produces type-safe, boilerplate-free component and system classes. The most widely used ECS framework in the Unity ecosystem.
score_rationale: The dominant Unity ECS framework with 7.6k stars and MIT license, though active development slowed after 2023 as Unity's DOTS gained traction — still widely used in existing projects.

name: genaray/Arch
description: High-performance C# archetype and chunks ECS framework with optional multithreading, supporting .NET Standard 2.1, .NET 6/8, Unity, and Godot. Focuses on cache efficiency and minimal allocations.
score_rationale: Best-in-class C# archetype ECS with 1.6k stars, Apache-2.0 licensed, actively maintained through May 2025, and growing adoption in Unity and Godot projects as a modern Entitas alternative.

name: sebas77/Svelto.ECS
description: Real ECS framework for C# using static archetypes and explicit group-based entity management for encapsulated, cache-friendly data-oriented design. Compatible with Unity, Godot, and .NET Standard 2.0+.
score_rationale: Solid C# ECS with 1.4k stars promoting strict data-oriented discipline, used in production games, and offering unique design patterns for maintainable ECS code.

name: scellecs/morpeh
description: ECS framework for Unity and .NET with a simple, struct-based API requiring no code generation and minimal setup. Offers cache-friendly storage and straightforward system/filter architecture.
score_rationale: Clean, no-codegen Unity ECS with 641 stars, MIT licensed, maintained through January 2025, appealing to developers who find Entitas boilerplate excessive.

name: ecsyjs/ecsy
description: Experimental Entity Component System framework for JavaScript/TypeScript designed to be lightweight, easy to use, and engine-agnostic for web-based game development.
score_rationale: Pioneer JavaScript ECS library with 1.2k stars and MIT license, but archived in April 2025 after the ecosystem moved toward more performant alternatives like bitECS.

name: fritzy/ape-ecs
description: Performant Entity-Component-System library for JavaScript with advanced entity queries, persistent indexes, component references, and 100% test coverage for game and simulation development.
score_rationale: Well-designed JavaScript ECS with 311 stars and MIT license but abandoned since November 2020, superseded by more active projects.

name: libretro/RetroArch
description: The reference frontend for the libretro API, providing a cross-platform emulator frontend that loads game systems as dynamic library cores. Supports real-time rewind, multi-pass shaders, video recording, and run-ahead latency reduction across dozens of platforms.
score_rationale: The industry-standard emulator frontend with 12.8k stars, underpinning the entire libretro ecosystem used by millions for retro gaming.

name: RPCS3/rpcs3
description: The world's first free and open-source PlayStation 3 emulator and debugger, written in C++ for Windows, Linux, macOS, and FreeBSD. Supports over 3500 games with active development.
score_rationale: Landmark open-source achievement with 18.4k stars; the definitive PS3 emulator maintained through early 2026 with broad game compatibility.

name: dolphin-emu/dolphin
description: A GameCube and Wii emulator for Windows, Linux, macOS, and Android, allowing play of games from those systems on PC with graphical improvements and enhancements over original hardware.
score_rationale: Legendary emulator with 14.8k stars and 45k+ commits; the definitive open-source GameCube/Wii emulator with decades of active development.

name: kitao/pyxel
description: A retro game engine for Python inspired by PICO-8 and TIC-80, featuring a 16-color palette, 4-channel audio, and built-in sprite/sound editors. Makes pixel-art game creation accessible to Python developers.
score_rationale: The most accessible retro fantasy console for Python developers with 17.4k stars, MIT-licensed and actively maintained.
